content:
erin: Customer reports SSO broke after IdP rotated signing certs ~08:12 UTC. They get a 400 on our ACS with 'InvalidRecipient' in the logs. They pasted their ACS as https://app.acme.example.com/saml/acs (no trailing slash).
erin: Ticket: CRO-4821. Customer says their IdP metadata was updated but they might have multiple hostnames behind a CDN.
devon: can you paste the raw SAML response error from our logs? need the Destination/Recipient fields.
erin: log snippet: 
```
Aug 12 08:14:02 saml-handler ERROR ValidateInResponseTo failed: InvalidRecipient - expected https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs/ got https://app.acme.example.com/saml/acs
```
erin: also saw this in the IdP SAML: Destination="https://app.acme.example.com/saml/acs" Recipient="https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs/"
maria: aha, looks like hostname aliasing + trailing slash mismatch. Our SP metadata lists ACS as https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs/ (with slash). If IdP issues Recipient without the slash it fails strict compare.
raj: customers often have CDN hostname rewrites. Also cert rotation could change EntityDescriptor KeyDescriptor order; signature validation can still pass but fingerprint checks fail if we cached old metadata. did we fetch new metadata for acme-idp?
support-bot: Metadata refresh job for acme-idp completed at 08:10 UTC (200 OK).
devon: can you reproduce from our side? try curl to the ACS with the Host header they use and post a minimal SAML response (or at least GET to ensure 302 behavior).
erin: repro steps I ran: 
```
curl -v -H "Host: app.acme.example.com" https://app.redwood.example.com/saml/acs -o /dev/null
* Connected to app.redwood.example.com (10.2.3.4)
> GET /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
> Host: app.acme.example.com
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
So Host header routed to our endpoint OK. But SAML library compares Destination/Recipient header values in the assertion exactly against our configured ACS URL (the one in SP metadata).
maria: quick fixes: 1) add alias entry in SP config to accept https://app.acme.example.com/saml/acs (no slash) OR 2) ask IdP admin to update Recipient to match SP ACS (add trailing slash) OR 3) relax strictRecipientMatching for this tenant (temporary, riskier).
raj: also check their metadata KeyDescriptor thumbprint. customer sent metadata, fingerpints: old=AB:12:34..., new=CD:56:78... Our cached copy was showing AB:12:34... until support-bot said refresh at 08:10 though. maybe there was a race between rotation and metadata fetch. Need to verify exact cert present in metadata we used to validate signature.
ere: small correction: the customer said signature validation failed intermittently (some log lines show 'Signature verification failed' and others show 'InvalidRecipient'). that implies mixed traffic hitting different IdP nodes with inconsistent configs.
raj: can we tail logs per request id? ask customer for SAMLRequest ID or sample request id from their side. also request IdP node list.
erin: asked customer for last saml_response id and sent them this curl to capture the POST: 
```
nc -l 9000 > /tmp/saml.dump
# then set their IdP to POST to our collector temporary URL
```
maria: operational suggestion: add the acme hostname (no-slash) to SP allowed ACS list and trigger a metadata refresh. I'll make the change in the tenant config (low-risk, reversible).
sre-oncall: note: we rolled certificate rotation for tenant-guard yesterday; if metadata fetch happens during a rotation window, some IdP nodes may still present old certs. I'll add a check to compare all KeyDescriptors across metadata endpoints.
support-bot: Change applied: allowed_acs_aliases updated for tenant acme -> ["https://app.acme.example.com/saml/acs"]. Rolling out within 30s.
erin: customer confirmed: after alias added, SAML assertions accepted. They still want us to coordinate a follow-up with their IdP to fully converge configs.
devon: follow-up items: 1) add detection for trailing-slash vs non-slash mismatch to provide clearer logs, 2) add pre-flight alias discovery during metadata import, 3) add cert rotation enforcement window docs for customers.
erin: escalating doc/work items to product and security for longer-term fix. tagging @maria and @raj to own follow-ups. :thumbsup:
